task: Translate the provided Figma node JSON structure into a clean Vue 3 Single File Component (SFC).

expected_json_wrapper.vue_code_raw:
<template>
  <button :class="{ 'bg-blue-500': isActive, 'bg-gray-300': !isActive }" @click="isActive = !isActive">
    <slot />
  </button>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue';

interface IButtonProps {
  modelValue: boolean;
}

const props = defineProps<IButtonProps>();
const emit = defineEmits<{(e: 'update:modelValue', value: boolean): void}>();

const isActive = computed({
  get: () => props.modelValue,
  set: (val) => emit('update:modelValue', val)
});
</script>

<style scoped>
button { position: relative; }
</style>

STYLE_MAPPING_RULES: 1. COLOR STRICTNESS & FALLBACK: If 'fills' with fractional RGB exists inside a node, you MUST multiply R, G, B by 255, convert to HEX, and apply it (e.g., bg-[#4b96c2]). IF 'fills' is empty, missing, or has no color object, you MUST generate a visually appealing modern color matching the component's context (e.g., standard text-gray-800 for descriptions, bg-blue-600 for primary actions).

2. GEOMETRY & PADDINGS: If layout properties ('padding*', 'itemSpacing', 'cornerRadius') are explicitly defined, strictly map them to Tailwind arbitrary values (e.g., p-[12px], rounded-[8px]). IF they are missing or equal to 0 but the element logically needs them (like padding inside a button or card), dynamically apply standard Tailwind layout classes (e.g., p-4, space-y-3, rounded-xl) to keep the UI beautiful.

3. INTERACTIVE STATES (OVERRIDES): If 'overrides' or 'states' object is provided for a node, dynamically bind those properties to the Vue reactive state (e.g., toggling classes based on isActive). If no states are provided in JSON, implement basic web-standard interactive hover/active states manually (e.g., hover:opacity-90, active:scale-[0.98]).
CRITICAL_RULES: NEVER use 'defineComponent', 'export default', or manual 'setup()' function. Mistral, this is Vue 3 <script setup lang="ts"> only!
All props must be defined via pure TypeScript interface: defineProps<I[ComponentName]Props>()
Two-way data binding must use a computed property with get/set that emits 'update:modelValue'.
